fixed.problem: [blocker] The PR executor replayed a dependency's commits. A single dependency was brought in by a fast-forward (no merge commit), the next run deleted DEPS_BASE_REF once no dependency was open and rebased onto main, so after a squash-merge of the dependency its commits were replayed (conflict) or, after a close, carried silently.

fixed.how: dependencyBase merges each dependency with --no-ff (GitOps.mergeFrom noFastForward) and records each held dependency as refs/forerunner/deps/<task id>; the marker is never removed while the branch holds a dependency (only a rebuild onto main without open deps removes it; a marker the branch does not hold is dropped as stale); execute()'s resume and post-run syncs and continueResolved's sync decide by holdsMergedWork (merge, never rebase); a run rebuilds a branch whose held dependency went away (merged by squash/rebase, closed, redone, cancelled) before and after the inner executor with git rebase --onto <new base> DEPS_BASE_REF (GitOps.rebaseOntoFrom), replaying only the task's own commits.

For a voided review that is not the safe or likely option (core-experience.md §3.8). The body's "or send it back" names no action the person can find: the done task offers Redo, and the user guide says Redo. merge-in-app could offer Merge and Redo here. The fixer already reported this.

Hardcoded branch name: rebuiltChangedSentence and request-words.ts rebuildTitle say "rebuilt onto main" whatever the repository's default branch is, which is untrue for master or trunk (writing rule 4). The path is rare: a squash after which the task's own change differs.

Stale card: "#9 was rebuilt without #8, which is being redone" stays on the card and the record after #8's redo is done again with the same PR head (bench redo-dep). The sentence was true when written, but reads stale afterwards.

Commit noise: with --no-ff, a chain's third task gets two "Build on ... (pull request #2)" merge commits (one from #3's history, one of its own), and after a rebuild a "Build on #3" merge commit reaches main. This shows on GitHub's Commits tab and in main's history; the content is correct.

PR words promise a button that does not exist yet: the dependent PR says "use Merge in Forerunner", but that button arrives only with merge-in-app (group 3). This matches the spec, but until group 3 merges the words promise a feature that does not exist (writing rule 9).

MergeRecordRepo.pin now moves a merged record back to queued for a different PR URL, without the state graph: MERGE_RECORD_TRANSITIONS still says merged: [], so the generated graph doc and the code disagree. The packages/state suite (SQLite and Postgres) has no case for the new behaviour; only the composed SQLite test (e) covers it.

Chain edge case: if the middle task of a chain is busy when the first one's squash is seen, the third is rebuilt onto main plus the middle task's old branch, which still holds the first task's pre-squash commits. Once the middle task is rebuilt, the third follows it (rebuiltTo) and is not rebuilt again, so its PR can keep those old commits. The file content stays correct.

No shared worktree lock: the worktree lock is private to pr-executor, so ReviewedPrMerge's own git steps in a task worktree (mergeChecked's update path) are not serialised with a rebuild of the same worktree. This is part of the known in-flight-merge gap the ADR names.
Upgrade gap: the owed rebuilds live in memory. Also, PRs the old watcher already marked closed in its cursor are never reported after an upgrade. Both are written in ADR 0111 or are upgrade-only.

Not this area: the Overview's Last result keeps "Left 3 reviewed pull requests for you to merge" after one of them was squash-merged (merge-in-app owns the result lines). A failed card shows "**Summary**" markdown (the polish area owns the sign-off card).
Not this area: Redo of a done task starts no session; I had to press Start.

fixed.how:
Root cause: agent/loop.ts kept only USAGE_LIMIT_CODE and 'unavailable' from a failed call, and agent/sdk.ts mapped every is_error result to provider_error. Changes:
- provider_auth now survives the loop. On the SDK path, isClaudeCodeRefusal (provider/usage-limit.ts) reads an authentication_failed assistant error, or a result that reads as a 401 or an expired sign-in. The mapping sits only in the enforcing branch, after budget-stop's drain.
- RouterTaskBilling.refuse (wiring/billing-pick.ts) marks the source: limits.refusedAt, refusedKey (credentialFingerprint: the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256, never the value) and refusedWhy. It writes a billing.refused audit row and files one Inbox card per source while the mark stands (session/credential-wait.ts fileRefusedCard, key credential:refused). The card's words are in request-words.ts: title 'Anthropic refused your API key' (or '... your Claude sign-in'), body 'Save a new one in Settings. The work that needs it waits and starts by itself then.', a 'Save a new key' link to /setup, no choices.
- VaultLedgerProbe reports `refused` while the vault holds the refused credential, and BillingRouter skips the source with SkipCode `refused`.
- RoutedProvider (chat, planning, reviews) marks the source the same way and makes the call once more on the next source.
- The executor rests or refuses the source, then words what really comes next (stoppedRunSentence plus nextCredential, a pick that only reads). The runner releases the claim without counting a try and never treats it as a passing error. It then either puts the task back at the head of the queue for the credential that takes over, or ends the session on the wait.
- Settings' billing order view gets blocked 'refused'. BillingOrderSection.tsx shows 'Refused: Anthropic did not accept this key. Save a new one under Accounts and keys'.
- Saving a new key in the setup assistant ends the mark at once and closes the card (SetupRoutesDeps.onClaudeCredentialSaved, then RuntimeApp.billing.waits.credentialSaved). A key saved another way (fr setup) ends it on the daemon's next scheduler tick, because the fingerprint no longer matches (takeReady).
